column1: # The differences between edition 2 and edition 3 GQT results the GQ 3 RFC sanctions.
# A row whose bullet starts with `open:` is a difference no Compatibility bullet names, awaiting an RFC decision; the job prints it as a warning.

column5: Both refuse `min` over a bare node name; edition 3 refuses at the word, since a bare identifier is not a value (section 5), where edition 2's type checker raised T8.
Edition 2's `delete T where` form stops compiling; it now fails with the statement-where parse error and its printed fix (Q008), where edition 2 refused the bare `false` with T46.

Both refuse a full-text call over a catalogue binding; `match_text` is respelled `match_terms`, whose refusal is the full-text code T27 (section 5: T27 stays the full-text code) where edition 2 used T23.
The operator catalogue lists the engine's operators; the new core adds seven and drops RankFuse.
The logical-kind catalogue follows the new core: seven kinds arrive, RankFuse and TextSearch leave.
The `engine` setting row is gone; `read_work_limit` and `plan_budget_limit` rows are added (additive).
The operator count follows the catalogue: 23 operators became 29.
The distinct operator identities follow the catalogue: 23 became 29.
Edition 2's step refused a search under `or` (T38); edition 3 accepts it, so the refusal step was removed.
Both refuse an aggregate compared in a filter; edition 3 names the aggregate rule (T8) where edition 2 raised the comparison code T7.
Both refuse `count` in a write's `where`; the write's `where` is a read's `where` in edition 3, which refuses the aggregate with T8 where edition 2 raised T44.
Both refuse a bare property name in a write; edition 3 refuses at the word, since a bare identifier is not a value (section 5), where edition 2 raised T45.
Both refuse a bare property name in an assignment; edition 3 refuses at the word, since a bare identifier is not a value (section 5), where edition 2 raised T45.
Edition 2 refused a search predicate in a write's `where` (T44); edition 3 accepts the lexical predicate there and the write succeeds.
Both refuse `count` in an assignment value; edition 3 names the aggregate rule (T8) where edition 2 raised T44.
A Boolean return item beside an aggregate, refused by edition 2 (T9), is accepted.
Both refuse list equality; the property brace becomes the equality `$x.tags = [...]`, refused by the comparison code T7 where edition 2's brace raised T3.
An order key that is not a return item, refused by edition 2 (T42), is accepted.
`knows{1,2}` from bob no longer returns bob through bob's self-loop.
The unaliased `nearest` column `p._distance` is `_distance`, the rename the respelling map carries.
The same row under the renamed `_distance` key; the distance is equal.
The unaliased `bm25` column `p._score` is `_score`, the rename the fixed map makes for `_distance`.
The same rows in the same order under the renamed `_score` key, the scores bm25_v1's F64 rather than Lance's F32 (results.bm25-f64).
The `bm25` score column is F64 where edition 2 gave Lance's F32; no row matches in either edition.
Both refuse `nearest` in `return`; a ranking written as a call is T65 with the `from` fix (section 5), where edition 2 raised T33.
Both refuse `nearest` in `return`; a ranking written as a call is T65 with the `from` fix (section 5), where edition 2 raised T33.
Both refuse `nearest` under an aggregate; a ranking written as a call is T65 (section 5), where edition 2 raised T32.
Both refuse a full-text call read as a value in `return`; edition 3 refuses the unlowered term with T86 (section 5), where edition 2 raised T35.
Both refuse projecting an order alias in `return`; edition 3 refuses the bare name at the word (section 5), where edition 2 raised T36.
A triple with neither end bound, refused by edition 2 (T5), is accepted.
A triple with neither end bound, refused by edition 2 (T5), is accepted.
A triple with neither end bound, refused by edition 2 (T5), is accepted.
A wildcard triple with neither end bound, refused by edition 2 (T5), is accepted.
Both refuse a parenthesized single edge used as a filter; edition 3 refuses it at parse with the fix `(a | b)`, where edition 2's type checker raised T41.
`(knows | likes){1,3}` from `a` no longer returns `a` through its self-loop.
Edition 2's step refused a block compared with an outer property (T40); edition 3 accepts it, so the refusal step was removed.
Both refuse an aggregate compared in a filter; edition 3 names the aggregate rule (T8, with the block as its fix) where edition 2 raised T7.
`avg` over integers that cancel is 0.5 exactly where edition 2's F64 accumulation returned 0.0.
Both refuse an aggregate compared in a filter; edition 3 names the aggregate rule (T8) where edition 2 raised T7.
Both refuse a property beside an aggregate that no item groups by; edition 3 raises T9 where edition 2 raised T58.
An order key over grouped rows that is a meta-field neither returned nor a key is refused.
An order key over grouped rows that is a meta-field neither returned nor a key is refused.
An order key over grouped rows that is a meta-field neither returned nor a key is refused.
Both refuse the unknown property `id`; edition 3 reports an unknown name with T6 (the freeze list: an unknown meta-field is a type error), where edition 2 raised T2.
Both refuse the unknown property `src`; edition 3 reports it with T6 where edition 2 raised T11.
Both refuse the unknown property `dst`; edition 3 reports it with T6 where edition 2 raised T11.
Both refuse an unknown meta-field; edition 3 reports it with T6 where edition 2 raised T11.
Both refuse an unknown meta-field; edition 3 reports it with T6 where edition 2 raised T11.
Both refuse the unknown property `id`; edition 3 reports it with T6 where edition 2 raised T11.
Edition 2's `set engine = v2` step has no counterpart: the setting is gone.
An `rrf` whose arms rank two bindings is a type error (T75, an rrf arm fault) where edition 2 raised T59.
An `rrf` whose arms rank two bindings is a type error (T75, an rrf arm fault) where edition 2 raised T59.
Both refuse `asc` on a `bm25` rank key; the ranking written in `order` is T65 through the code map (section 6), where edition 2 raised T54.
Both refuse `asc` on an `rrf` rank key; the ranking written in `order` is T65 through the code map (section 6), where edition 2 raised T54.
Edition 2's `set engine = v2` step has no counterpart: the setting is gone.
Edition 2's `show engine` step has no counterpart: the setting is gone.
Both refuse a Date aggregate compared with a number; T40 no longer restricts a block's partner (section 5), so the comparison code T7 refuses it.
Edition 2's `fuzzy` asked Lance's index, whose default tokenizer matched nothing (the case's documented limitation); edition 3's exact scan finds the two titles within two edits.
`max` of 2^53+1 compared with the float literal 2^53 compares as F64, where both round to 2^53, so the row no longer qualifies.
2^53+1 compared with the float literal 2^53 compares as F64, where both round to 2^53.
An edge's 2^53+1 compared with the float literal 2^53 compares as F64, where both round to 2^53.
The projected comparison of 2^53+1 with the float literal 2^53 is false in F64.
Membership of the float literal 2^53 in a list holding 2^53+1 compares as F64, where both round to 2^53.
Membership of 2^53+1 in a list of the float literal 2^53 compares as F64, where both round to 2^53.
Both refuse a negative edit budget; edition 3 refuses the option out of range at type check (T71, section 5) where edition 2 failed at run time.
Both refuse an oversized edit budget; edition 3 refuses the option out of range at type check (T71, section 5) where edition 2 failed at run time.
